title: Safe changes, tolerant readers and upcasting
summary: Which changes are safe, how a tolerant reader survives the rest, how versioned event types and upcasters handle breaking changes, and the deploy order that keeps traffic flowing.

steps.title: Safe and breaking changes
body: | Change | Verdict | Why |
| Add an optional field **with a default** | safe | old data reads with the default; old readers ignore it |
| Remove a field that **has** a default | safe | readers that still want it use the default |
| Rename a field | **breaking** | to a schema it is a remove plus an add (Avro `aliases` help readers only) |
| Change a type (`int` → `string`) | **breaking** | except promotions such as Avro `int` → `long` |
| Make an optional field required | **breaking** | old data has no value |
| Change the **meaning** (euros → cents, same name and type) | **breaking** | and no checker will catch it |
**Protobuf** is matched by field **number**, not name:
```text
message OrderPlaced {
reserved 4;            // coupon was removed: nobody may reuse 4
reserved "coupon";     // ...or the old name, for JSON mapping
string order_id = 1;
int64 total_cents = 2;
string currency = 3;
string gift_note = 5;  // new fields get NEW numbers
Reusing a number makes old bytes decode into the wrong field, silently. Renaming is wire-safe in binary but breaks
the JSON mapping (`order_id` becomes `orderId` in JSON).

steps.prompt: Safe or breaking for existing consumers?
items: Remove `coupon`, which has a default of `null`
Drop the default from `currency` so it is required
Send `total` in cents instead of euros, same name and type
Protobuf: give field number 4 to a new `gift_note`
explain: The unit change is the nastiest: every schema check passes, every consumer deserializes happily, and the invoices
are off by a factor of 100. Contract tests that assert **values** catch what schema checks cannot.

steps.title: Tolerant readers and versioned event types
body: A **tolerant reader** reads only the fields it needs, ignores unknown ones, defaults missing optional ones, and maps
unknown enum values to a fallback instead of throwing. Producers can then add fields without a coordinated deploy.
- `System.Text.Json` ignores unknown properties by default. `JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow` (.NET 8+) makes it
strict: right for validating a public API request, wrong for an event consumer.
- `JsonStringEnumConverter` throws on an unknown enum string; read the value as a string and map unknowns yourself.
When a change **is** breaking, do not mutate the contract in place. Version it:
- a new type name (`shop.order.placed.v2`) or a new topic (`orders.v2`);
- during the migration the producer publishes both, or consumers **upcast**: convert an old version to the newest
one on read, so the handler only ever sees the latest shape. Event-sourced systems do this all the time, because
stored events are never rewritten.

steps.prompt: Ten minutes after `orders-api` 3.4 shipped, `shipping-worker` started dead-lettering every message with this log line. What is the cause?
code: System.Text.Json.JsonException: The JSON property 'giftWrap' could not be mapped to any .NET member
options: The consumer is a strict reader (unmapped members disallowed): the producer added a field, which should be a safe change
explain: Adding a field is the textbook safe change, and only a strict reader turns it into an outage. Fix the reader
(drop `UnmappedMemberHandling = Disallow`, or read with `JsonDocument`), replay the dead-lettered messages, and add a
contract test that feeds the consumer a message with an extra field.

steps.title: Make the reader tolerant
prompt: **Symptom.** Since the producer started sending `giftWrap`, and some older producers never send `currency`, the
reader below throws on most messages and shipping has 14,000 dead letters.
Fix `OrderPlaced Read(string json)` so it is a **tolerant reader**:
- `orderId` and `totalCents` are required: throw `JsonException` if either is missing;
- unknown properties are ignored;
- `currency` is optional and defaults to `"EUR"`;
- `channel` is optional; anything other than `"web"` or `"app"` (including missing) becomes `"other"`.
The tests define `record OrderPlaced(string OrderId, int TotalCents, string Currency, string Channel);`
starter: string? orderId = null, currency = null, channel = null;
default: throw new JsonException($"The JSON property '{p.Name}' could not be mapped to any member of OrderPlaced.");
if (orderId is null || currency is null || channel is null) throw new JsonException("missing required property");
if (channel is not ("web" or "app")) throw new JsonException($"unknown channel '{channel}'");
return new OrderPlaced(orderId, total, currency, channel);
solution: if (!root.TryGetProperty("orderId", out var id) || id.GetString() is not string orderId)
throw new JsonException("missing required property orderId");
throw new JsonException("missing required property totalCents");
var currency = root.TryGetProperty("currency", out var c) ? c.GetString() ?? "EUR" : "EUR";
var channel = root.TryGetProperty("channel", out var ch) ? ch.GetString() : null;
return new OrderPlaced(orderId, total.GetInt32(), currency, channel);
hints: Stop looping over every property: ask for the ones you need with `TryGetProperty`.
Keep throwing for the two required fields; everything else gets a default.
template: Dojo.Eq("a new field is ignored", new OrderPlaced("o-2", 500, "EUR", "app"), Read("""{"orderId":"o-2","totalCents":500,"currency":"EUR","channel":"app","giftWrap":true}"""));
Dojo.Eq("missing currency defaults to EUR", new OrderPlaced("o-3", 700, "EUR", "web"), Read("""{"orderId":"o-3","totalCents":700,"channel":"web"}"""));
Dojo.Eq("an unknown channel becomes other", new OrderPlaced("o-4", 100, "EUR", "other"), Read("""{"orderId":"o-4","totalCents":100,"currency":"EUR","channel":"kiosk"}"""));
Dojo.Eq("a missing channel becomes other", new OrderPlaced("o-5", 100, "EUR", "other"), Read("""{"orderId":"o-5","totalCents":100}"""));
record OrderPlaced(string OrderId, int TotalCents, string Currency, string Channel);

steps.title: Deploy order
body: Who deploys first depends on the change:
```text
additive change (add optional field with a default)
tolerant consumers ─► any order works
registry in BACKWARD mode ─► consumers first is the textbook order
breaking change (rename, type change, unit change): expand, migrate, contract
1  define shop.order.placed.v2 next to v1            (expand)
2  consumers learn v2 and upcast v1 → v2 ─► deploy
3  producer publishes v2 (or both v1 and v2)
4  watch v1 traffic reach zero, every consumer group caught up
5  stop publishing v1, delete the v1 path              (contract)
The question a reviewer asks: "if the producer goes out first and the consumer deploy is rolled back, what happens
to the messages in between?" With expand / migrate / contract the answer is "nothing".

steps.prompt: Put the rollout of a breaking change (`total` in euros becomes `totalCents`) in order.
lines: Teach every consumer to read v2 and upcast v1 to v2
Make the producer publish v2 (or both versions)
Wait until v1 traffic is zero and every consumer group has caught up
Stop publishing v1 and delete the v1 code path
explain: Consumers before producers: at no moment does a message exist that nobody can read. The waiting step matters on
Kafka, where v1 records stay in the log until retention removes them, and a replay will hit them.

steps.prompt: An upcaster chain runs on an old event. What does this print?
code: var steps = new Dictionary<int, Func<Dictionary<string, string>, Dictionary<string, string>>>
while (steps.TryGetValue(v, out var up)) { e = up(e); v++; }
explain: Each step upgrades one version, so the chain works from any starting version. But the v1 step copied the old
dictionary and never removed `total`: a handler that still reads `total` would keep working by accident. Decide

steps.title: An upcaster
prompt: Events arrive as flat dictionaries of strings. Write `Dictionary<string, string> Upcast(Dictionary<string, string> e)`
that returns the event as **version 3**, without changing the input dictionary:
- `version` is read from `e["version"]`; a missing `version` means 1.
- **v1 → v2**: `total` (euros, like `"12.50"`, invariant culture) becomes `totalCents` (`"1250"`); `total` is removed.
- **v2 → v3**: `customer` is renamed to `customerId` (if present).
- The result has `version` = `"3"`; every other key is kept.
- A version below 1 or above 3 throws `NotSupportedException` with the message `"unknown version {n}"`: a consumer
must not guess at a future format (park it instead).
solution: var version = x.TryGetValue("version", out var v) ? int.Parse(v) : 1;
if (version < 1 || version > 3) throw new NotSupportedException($"unknown version {version}");
if (x.Remove("customer", out var customer)) x["customerId"] = customer;
hints: Copy first: `var x = new Dictionary<string, string>(e);`
Run the steps in sequence: `if (version == 1) { ...; version = 2; }` then `if (version == 2) { ...; version = 3; }`.
`x.Remove("customer", out var c)` removes and returns the value in one call.
template: string DojoShow(Dictionary<string, string> d) => string.Join(",", d.OrderBy(k => k.Key, StringComparer.Ordinal).Select(k => $"{k.Key}={k.Value}"));
Dojo.Eq("the input is not changed", "customer=c-9,orderId=o-1,total=12.50,version=1", DojoShow(dojoV1));
Dojo.Throws<NotSupportedException>("a future version is not guessed at", () => Upcast(new() { ["version"] = "4", ["orderId"] = "o-6" }));

steps.title: Read any version
prompt: Put it together. Write `OrderV3 ReadAny(string json)` for the shipping consumer:
1. parse the JSON object into a `Dictionary<string, string>`: string values as their text, any other value as its
raw JSON text (`12.5`, `1`, `true`);
2. `Upcast` it to v3 (your upcaster is already in the editor);
3. return `new OrderV3(orderId, totalCents, customerId, currency)` as a **tolerant reader**: unknown keys are
ignored, `currency` defaults to `"EUR"`, `customerId` defaults to `""`.
An unknown version keeps throwing `NotSupportedException` from `Upcast`.
The tests define `record OrderV3(string OrderId, int TotalCents, string CustomerId, string Currency);`
starter: var version = x.TryGetValue("version", out var v) ? int.Parse(v) : 1;
if (version < 1 || version > 3) throw new NotSupportedException($"unknown version {version}");
if (x.Remove("customer", out var customer)) x["customerId"] = customer;
solution: var version = x.TryGetValue("version", out var v) ? int.Parse(v) : 1;
if (version < 1 || version > 3) throw new NotSupportedException($"unknown version {version}");
if (x.Remove("customer", out var customer)) x["customerId"] = customer;
hints: After `Upcast`, read with `GetValueOrDefault(key, fallback)` for the optional fields.
template: Dojo.Eq("a v1 message with an extra field", new OrderV3("o-1", 1250, "c-9", "EUR"), ReadAny("""{"version":1,"orderId":"o-1","total":12.5,"customer":"c-9","giftWrap":true}"""));
Dojo.Eq("a v3 message with a currency", new OrderV3("o-3", 800, "c-3", "SEK"), ReadAny("""{"version":3,"orderId":"o-3","totalCents":800,"customerId":"c-3","currency":"SEK"}"""));
Dojo.Eq("version as a string, no customer", new OrderV3("o-4", 300, "", "EUR"), ReadAny("""{"version":"1","orderId":"o-4","total":"3.00"}"""));
record OrderV3(string OrderId, int TotalCents, string CustomerId, string Currency);
